slides.text: The `maps` package does for maps what `slices` does for slices: copying, deleting by a rule and collecting keys and values. You will also put both packages together.

`maps.Keys` gives the keys of a map, but in the random order of a `range`, and not as a slice. To get a slice you can trust, wrap it in `slices.Sorted`, which collects the keys and sorts them.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
keys = keys of the map (any order)
list = keys put in order

slides.text: A sorted list of keys is how you read a map in a fixed order: loop over the keys, and look each one up. `maps.Clone` and `maps.Equal` do for maps what `slices.Clone` and `slices.Equal` do for slices.

exercises.explanation: `maps.Keys` gives the keys in random order, and `slices.Sorted` collects them into a sorted slice, so the order is always the same.

slides.text:
`maps.Copy(dst, src)` writes every entry of one map into another, overwriting keys they share. It changes `dst`, so use `maps.Clone` first when you need a new map.

`maps.DeleteFunc` removes the entries that fit a rule, and the rule gets both the key and the value.

`maps.Values` and `maps.Keys` are not slices. Wrap them in `slices.Sorted`, or in `slices.Collect` when the order does not matter. Printing a map with `fmt` is always in key order, but looping over it is not.

exercises.title: Copy into a map
exercises.guide: Write the entries of one map into another.

chunks.guide: Two maps that share the key `b`. The imports are already in the file.
`maps.Copy(dst, src)` writes every entry of `src` into `dst`. A key that `dst` already has gets the new value.
The source is not changed.
Clone first when the original must stay as it is.
chunks.text:
merged := maps.Clone(base)
    maps.Copy(merged, map[string]int{"d": 4})
    fmt.Println(len(merged), len(base))

slides.text:
Real code mixes the two packages. A map has no order, so to show it ranked you collect its keys into a slice, sort that slice with a rule that looks each key up in the map, and then walk the slice.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
keys = the keys of the map
sort keys by: value of the key, then key
for each key in keys:
    show key and its value
